q-41328.name: Question 1
q-41328.problem: Find the value of $\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{3+3y-6x}$ when $x=-4$ and $y=3.$
q-41328.worked_solution:
We replace $x$ with $-4$ and $y$ with $3$ in the given expression, and simplify as much as possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{3+3y-6x} & = \\ \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{3+3\cdot 3-6\cdot (-4)} & = \\ \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{3+9+24} & = \\ \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{36} & = \\ \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{{6}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot 6 & = \\ 2\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Find the value of 133+3y−6x when x=−4 and y=3.

a
 2
b
 9
c
 6
d

e
 3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We replace x with −4 and y with 3 in the given expression, and simplify as much as possible: 133+3y−6x=133+3⋅3−6⋅(−4)=133+9+24=1336=1362=13⋅6=2

q-110877.name: Question 3
q-110877.problem: Find the value of $\sqrt{3x+5y}$ when $x=1$ and $y=5.$
q-110877.worked_solution:
We replace $x$ with $1$ and $y$ with $5$ in the given expression, and simplify as much as possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3x+5y} & = \\ \sqrt{3(1)+5(5)} & = \\ \sqrt{3+25} & = \\ \sqrt{28} & = \\ \sqrt{4\cdot 7} & = \\ \sqrt{{2}^{2}\cdot 7} & = \\ \sqrt{{2}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{7} & = \\ 2\sqrt{7}\end{aligned}
$$

q-110876.name: Question 4
q-110876.worked_solution:
We replace $x$ with $18$ in the given expression, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{x+6} & = \\ \sqrt{18+6} & = \\ \sqrt{24}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify even further using the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{24} & = \\ \sqrt{4\cdot 6} & = \\ \sqrt{{2}^{2}\cdot 6} & = \\ \sqrt{{2}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{6} & = \\ 2\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

q-110880.name: Question 6
q-110880.worked_solution:
We replace $x$ with $4$ in the given expression, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) & =\frac{\sqrt{2(4)+1}}{\sqrt{4}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8+1}}{\sqrt{4}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{9}}{\sqrt{4}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-63879.name: Question 8
q-63879.worked_solution:
We replace $t$ with $7$ in the given expression, and simplify as much as possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3t+4}-\sqrt[3]{9t+1} & = \\ \sqrt{3\cdot 7+4}-\sqrt[3]{9\cdot 7+1} & = \\ \sqrt{21+4}-\sqrt[3]{63+1} & = \\ \sqrt{25}-\sqrt[3]{64} & = \\ \sqrt{{5}^{2}}-\sqrt[3]{{4}^{3}} & = \\ 5-4 & = \\ 1 & \end{aligned}
$$
